A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3D Half-Gaussian Splatting work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original rendering experiments, kernel comparisons, and image analyses, including Tables 2–4 and appendix scene-level results.

after.justification: V4 retains original rendering results and adds scene-level scores, geometric diagnostics, training-time analysis, and a rasterizer ablation.

M1.justification: The paired half-Gaussian kernel, learned splitting plane and opacities, integration formula, efficient splatting procedure, and Algorithm 1 are retained. Revised explanations and the preliminary alpha-blending equation correction do not establish a changed proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: V4 adds Flowers and Treehill rendering evaluations in appendix Table 4 and a drums-scene comparison of splitting-plane normals with ground-truth surface normals in C.2. The original three benchmark datasets and their previously evaluated scenes remain.

E2.justification: The existing external-baseline and reconstruction-kernel comparison sets are unchanged. Appendix C.4 newly evaluates 3D-HGS without the efficient rasterizer against the complete system, adding an internal comparison variant.

E3.justification: V4 introduces a Bonsai comparison against elapsed training time and a with/without-rasterizer control on a single RTX 3090. Its revised Bonsai diagnostic reports absolute-error traces and normalized image-wide error maps. Existing benchmark training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 substantially expands the diagnostic evidence: C.2 examines geometric alignment, C.3 compares quality and kernel counts against training time, and C.4 isolates the efficient rasterizer's contribution. Figure 7 also expands v3's Bonsai column-fitting analysis with error traces and full-image error maps.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or experimental uncertainty estimates. The added curves and tables continue reporting point results.

E6.justification: Corresponding main tables retain identical numerical results. V4 adds Flowers/Treehill scores and geometric, training-time, and rasterizer-ablation findings. New Table 5 reports 76/125, 95/160, and 82/126 FPS without/with the efficient rasterizer across the three datasets; these are new condition-specific comparisons, not improvements over v3's scores.

T1.justification: V4 corrects Eq. 6's transmittance factor from i−σ_j to 1−σ_j and consistently defines effective opacity σ_i. It specifies positive-definite covariance matrices and corrects standard-deviation terminology. V3's kernel-formula summary table is removed, while Appendix A's derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both retain the plug-and-play kernel contribution, state-of-the-art rendering-quality claim, and applicability across four Gaussian-splatting architectures without compromising rendering speed. The shortened abstract and conclusion preserve these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2 newly interprets splitting-plane/surface-normal alignment as evidence that half-ellipsoids represent sharp transitions between surfaces and empty space, linking this to transparent kernel halves. Section 3.4 also makes the transparency-based efficiency explanation more explicit.

D1.justification: V4 adds training-time information with 7K/30K iteration checkpoints and per-dataset kernel counts in C.3–C.4. Existing implementation pseudocode, learning rates, opacity thresholds, hardware disclosure, and project/code access information are retained.

R1.justification: The same 35 referenced works and substantive research positioning are retained, including the distinctions from 2D-GS and GES. Removing a duplicate FlashGS citation from B.1 does not change the retained attribution in Section 3.4.

P1.justification: V4 substantially shortens the abstract, lightly edits the conclusion and method explanations, removes redundant introductory text from B.1, and reorganizes Appendix C into subsections. Author contact and funding text are added; most existing prose and section organization remain.

P2.justification: The visual evidence is substantially expanded and revised: Figure 6 gains clearer bounding-region annotations, v3 Figure 9 becomes the multi-panel error Figure 7, and Figures 10–11 and an ablation table are added. The kernel-formula table is removed, the scene-results table expands, and pipeline/opacity figures are relocated.

improvement.justification: The new rasterizer ablation, geometric diagnostic, and training-time analysis strengthen support for the existing method, while the corrected Eq. 6 and clearer figures improve exposition. These are targeted gains rather than a change to the central results. A remaining reporting inconsistency is that Flowers/Treehill are added outside the unchanged seven-scene average despite C.1 describing averages as covering all scenes.
